study type: Longitudinal observational study with cross-sectional comparisons
exposure: Milk consumption type (human milk at breast, pumped human milk in bottle, traditional lactose-based formula, lactose-reduced formula with added sugar)
cohort: The study included 91 Hispanic infants who consumed human milk (at breast or pumped) or two kinds of infant formula (traditional lactose-based or lactose-reduced with added sugar).
finding: Infants consuming formula, particularly lactose-reduced formula with added sugar, exhibited a significantly more 'mature' microbiome with reduced Bifidobacteriaceae, increased Lachnospiraceae, and higher propionate compared to human milk-fed infants.
mod_finding: Consumption of infant formula with added sugar showed a stronger association with the infant's microbiome at 6 months of age compared to birth delivery mode.
